quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This is important in areas where hazards may appear.

questions.question: What should you do when riding through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay in the left part of the lane.
Always stay in the right part of the lane.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to move your position in the lane when needed. The best path through a curve does not always match the curve of the road.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from having to speed up to catch the group. It also lets experienced riders watch over them.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips less than five miles long at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: Helmeted riders are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash than not wearing one, at any speed.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn in a previous crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a previous crash.
questions.explanation: The best helmet protection comes from one that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, which part of the lane is usually best?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection when riding?

options.text: Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
No, not if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Hearing protection helps block this noise while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the car ahead.
Someone is sitting in a parked car's driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians who may move into your path. Use it when passing a car with someone in the driver's seat, a pedestrian, or a cyclist. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: Riders use signals to communicate when riding in groups. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride on the left side of your lane because:

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It helps you see hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane when passing gives you a better view. You can see farther ahead and oncoming traffic can see you better.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds behind other vehicles. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving right toward the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Moving left may make them merge back too quickly. The center position is safest.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: In traffic, stay in your lane if a small animal appears. Swerving into other lanes can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about 70 percent of your total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a rider do?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Use the horn repeatedly at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes reducing your speed, increasing your following distance, and using high beam headlights when safe. Adjust your lane position to stay visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders when looking through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, turn only your head to look through the turn. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance at night?
questions.explanation: At night, visibility is reduced and judging distance is harder. Maintain a minimum following distance of three seconds. You need extra time to react and stop if the vehicle ahead brakes.

questions.question: What is the best riding formation for a group?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Switch to single-file when turning, riding curves, or entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have rounded, or convex, mirrors. What do these mirrors do?

options.text: They are easy to get used to right away.
They make cars look closer than they really are.
They show a narrow view of the road.
They make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they actually are. If you are new to convex mirrors, practice judging distances.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcycle riders pass on a two-lane highway?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders in a group should pass one at a time. The lead rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when exiting a highway?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for normal group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What formation is best for a group entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for general group riding. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If a rider must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should they do?

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time with extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good traction to swerve safely, so do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is used.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is used.
Applies equal braking to both brakes when either is used.
Remembers and learns your normal braking force.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies partial front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Who should set the pace for a group of riders?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the pace. This makes sure no riders get left behind.

questions.question: When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points it upward, what does this mean?

options.text: They are about to slow down.

questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show turns or stops. When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points it upward, they are signaling a right turn or right lane change.
